Writes the EEPROM mirror 0x803b0a-0x804155 back to the EEPROM: 7 while not_safe_to_program_flag is 1; else 16-byte chunks through cm550_circularBufferWrite (the EEPROM byte write queue) with up to 16000 waits for the queue each; 0. The same function as CM848 0x21918 (shared name; was cm550_FUN_00011a74; PR #53 round 73).

The discrete input sampler and debouncer - nothing in it concerns injector timing: it reads the chip select 2 device's input bytes 0xFFD000-0xFFD003 / 0xFFD005 / 0xFFD007 and SIM_PORTE0 / SIM_PORTF0 - XORs them with the polarity masks into three 4-sample rings - debounces each byte as (AND of 4) | (OR of 4 & previous) - then decodes the PTO and cruise switches with 25-pass hold counters and two 50-pass switch-pair faults (was injectorTimingCalculation; PR #53 round 85)

Drains the J1708 receive buffer for at most 500 CTM4_BIUTBR ticks: first it sends the deferred reply commitEepromMirrorToEeprom arms (once the EEPROM write queue is empty); each record is [length][message bytes] and the first message byte picks the handler (3 = the 10-byte key through validateSecurityKey and then commands 0x40-0x54 - 4 = control commands 0x64-0x76 - 5 = memory read / write / multipacket). Its old shared name came from a pairing CM848 later dropped (was diagnosticCommandDispatcher; PR #53 round 85)

Starts a J1708 transmission: with a message pending and the bus idle (QSM_SCSR bit 0x20 RAF clear) it writes the first byte to QSM_SCDR - arms the timer at 0xFFF458 / 0xFFF45A (the CTM4 address range) and sets QSM_SCCR1 RIE to read back its own bytes (the J1708 collision check). It drives no TPU channel (was mc68k_tpuTransmissionTrigger; PR #53 round 75)

Sets up TPU channel 10 for the primary speed sensor and fills its pulse period table (pulse_period_table_table_containing_main_speed_pulse_per_1000_65535): parameter 1 = DAT_00807ecc << 8 - parameter 0 = 0xb - HSQR0 bits 0x30 - handler mc68k_tpuChannel10PrimarySpeedInterruptHandlerMode0. The other mode is mc68k_initializeTpuChannel10PrimarySpeedInputIfEnabled. No CAN register is involved (was mc68k_can1TimerBufferInitDivided; PR #53 round 82)

The TPU channel 10 (primary engine speed sensor) interrupt handler for speed_measurement_mode 0 (saves d0-d1 / a0-a5 and ends in RTE): it reads the 32-bit pulse period from channel 10 parameters 4-5 and clears parameter 4 - updates the pulse period ring with its per-cam and per-cylinder sums - the tooth counter and the lost-sensor timeout - checks the cylinder identification pulse - then runs the main / backup phase comparator and clears TPU_CISR bit 10 (was vp44_rpmTimerInterruptHandler2; PR #53 round 85)

Sets up TPU channel 0 (its CIER / HSRR1 bits and parameters 2-6) for the missing-tooth wheel input: it uses pmm_ratio_tooth_spacing_at_which_missing_tooth_is_found_0_1_9921875 / pmm_num_of_teeth_correct_tooth_count_at_missing_tooth_0_255 / tooth_count_at_which_missing_tooth_not_detct_err_0_255. No CAN register is involved (was mc68k_can1MessageTransmitInit2; PR #53 round 82)

It is the handler the dumped ECU runs (RAM 0x808F04 = 0x19E90) (was vp44_FUN_00019e90; PR #53 round 85)

The TPU channel 10 primary speed interrupt handler for speed_measurement_mode 2: ROM 0x1A52C-0x1A6E7 is the same 444 bytes as the mode 0 handler (0x19ACC-0x19C87); only its set-up differs (channel 10 parameter 1 from the per-cam pulse count

The TPU channel 10 primary speed interrupt handler for speed_measurement_mode 3 (saves d0-d3 / a0-a1 and ends in RTE): it reads the period and the edge time TPU_CH10_PARAM2 - clears parameter 4 - passes them to cm550_throttleTimeAccumulatorProcessor (in fact the mode 3 period ring / sync gap processor) - re-arms channel 10 (parameter 0 and HSR 2) - then runs the same phase comparator tail (was vp44_FUN_0001a8a4; PR #53 round 85)

Sets up TPU channel 1 (CFSR3 bits 7-4 / CIER bit 1 / HSRR1 bits 3-2 / parameters 0-3) for the backup speed sensor and fills its pulse period table (pulse_period_table_backup_* / period_meas_per_cam_backup_* / _teeth_per_cam_rev_backup_*). No CAN register is involved (was mc68k_dutyCycleMonitorAltCanInit; PR #53 round 82)

Flash block erase - run only from the 2 KB stack copy cm550_flashEraseFromRam makes: it writes 0x2020 / 0xD0D0 (erase set-up / confirm) to *flash_target_address_ptr and polls the status word for bit 7 up to 40000 times. Returns 0 erased / 1 erase error (status bit 5) or timeout / 2 suspended (0xB0B0) when the suspend check is on and bit 0 of the chip select 2 device's register 0 reads 1 on 4 consecutive reads. The .cpp drops the 0 path and the status commands - read ROM 0x1C354 onward. mc68k_ for the 0xFFD000 read (was cm550_flashEraseWithWatchdog; PR #53 round 85)

The erase runner - the erase twin of cm550_flashProgramFromRam: it stores the block address in flash_target_address_ptr and the suspend flag at 0x8006A6 (1 = never suspend: the boot block; 0 from the parameter block savers)
column4: copies mc68k_flashEraseBlock (0x1C31A-0x1C483) into a 2 KB stack buffer and calls the copy. Returns its result: 0 erased / 1 error or timeout / 2 suspended (was cm550_FUN_0001c484; PR #53 round 85)

column3: The RAM-run flash programmer (run only from the stack copy cm550_flashProgramFromRam makes): for each word up to the end pointer at 0x8006A2 it writes 0x4040 and the source word - polls the status up to 5000 times - accepts the word only when status & 0xF8F8 = 0x0080 and the read-back matches - and retries a failed word up to 5 times. Returns 1 all words programmed / 0 a word failed (the .cpp's 'return 0' on both exits is wrong). Its only hardware access is the inline watchdog kick
column4: so not mc68k_ (commit 16143a5c) (was cm550_flashProgramWordWithWatchdog; PR #53 round 85)

column3: The interrupt handler of the 82527 CAN controller on chip select 4: loops while CAN_CS4_INTERRUPT is non-zero - on a status change it reads CAN_CS4_STATUS and resets the controller (CAN_CS4_CONTROL = 1 / waits for CAN_CS4_CPU_INTERFACE bit 7 / restores the control bits) - and passes message object interrupts to cm550_serialNodeAddressForwarder / cm550_serialNodeAddressChecker (was cm550_FUN_0001e0fa; PR #53 round 81)

The interrupt handler of the 82527 CAN controller on chip select 5: loops while CAN_CS5_INTERRUPT is non-zero - codes below 3 are the status change / message 15 cases (reads CAN_CS5_STATUS and resets CAN_CS5_CONTROL) - code n reaches message object n - 2 at CAN_CS5_INTERRUPT * 0x10 + 0xffc7e0. No serial port is involved (was mc68k_serialPort2IsrHandler; PR #53 round 79)

Arms the J1708 bus timer: sets j1708_bus_timer_armed_flag - loads CTM4_MCSM11CNT with 0xfc8a - clears CTM4_MCSM11SIC bit 15 and sets its bit 14 (an interrupt level). It drives no TPU channel and takes no parameter (was mc68k_tpuTimerChannelEnable; PR #53 round 77)

The J1708 SCI interrupt handler: on QSM_SCSR RDRF (0x40) it reads the byte from QSM_SCDR into the J1708 receive buffer and adds it to the checksum - while transmitting it sends the next transmit byte to QSM_SCDR and at the end the two's complement of the checksum (~sum + 1) - and it clears QSM_SCCR1 RIE when the receive buffer is full. No EPS position sensor is involved (was mc68k_epsPositionSensorIsrHandler; PR #53 round 75)

Sends the next frame on the 82527 CAN controller on chip select 4: writes a message object's control register through _can_control_register_pointer - copies the next 14-byte entry of the CAN transmit ring (0x80D896-0x80D9A0) with cm550_canFrameDataCopy(&CAN_CS4_CONTROL) and advances the ring pointer. No serial port is involved (was serialTransmitHandler; PR #53 round 81)

Copies the frame in message object n of the chip select 4 82527 (n = the low byte of its word argument) into the next 18-byte entry of the CAN receive ring: the identifier (arbitration >> 3) - the length - a pointer to the entry's data - the 8 data bytes. Objects 1-14 are re-read while control 1 bit 1 is set again; object 15 is read at 0xFFD8F2 / 0xFFD8F6 / 0xFFD8F7. The ring wraps from past 0x80D884 to 0x80D72E (was cm550_FUN_0001e5f0; PR #53 round 85)

Writes memory for a PGN 61184 write request (services 0x4b / 0x4d): a length cap of 1764 / an optional 10-byte key after the data / the region from lookupApplicationMemoryRegionType - 0 copied / 3 copied after validateSecurityKey (3 when the key is missing or refused) / 4 refused (10) / 5 EEPROM: 7 while not safe to program with RAM refresh on then the key (0x1a missing / 3 refused) then cm550_circularBufferWrite (0x0b when full) and the mirror copy / the other codes passed back. The same function as CM848 0x50af58 (shared name - CM848 returns 0x1a for a type 3 write without the key / refuses (10) type 3 writes into its calibration RAM while RAM refresh is on / has Bank 2; was cm550_memoryOperationDispatcher; PR #53 round 72).

PGN 61184 service 0x4b: request bytes 1-4 the address and 5 the length then the data - written through writeJ1939DiagnosticMemory. The same function as CM848 0x50b408 (shared name; was cm550_memoryOperationFromMessageExtended; PR #53 round 72).

PGN 61184 service 0x4d: request bytes 1-4 the address and 5-8 the length then the data - written through writeJ1939DiagnosticMemory. The same function as CM848 0x50b474 (shared name; was cm550_FUN_00021826; PR #53 round 72).

The request bytes before the data for a PGN 61184 memory service: 0 below 0x41 else j1939_memory_service_header_lengths[service - 0x41] (read from its base 0x21915). The same function and table as CM848 0x50b610 / 0x53a322 (shared name; was cm550_addressLookupFunction; PR #53 round 72).

The serial EEPROM driver over the QSPI: issues the SPI EEPROM commands 5 (read status - tests the write-in-progress bit in QSM_RR3) / 6 (write enable) / 2 (write) / 3 (read). Each write sends the next queue entry: the address word at 0x80BDA8 + 2 x eeprom_circular_buffer_read_index (QSM_TR4) and the data byte at 0x80C7A8 + index (QSM_TR5). No QADC register is involved (was mc68k_qadcDataCollectionStateMachine; PR #53 round 81)

Services both watchdogs and re-samples the discrete inputs - adds 1 to the completed power-down count (0x803FEC) and queues the EEPROM write - waits up to 1000 passes - writes the power cycle sequence number 0x803FE2 = the incomplete count (0x803FEA) + the completed count - waits again - and jumps to the application main's restart entry 0x28978. CM848's cm848_restartOnKeyOnDuringPowerDown runs the same steps. Its only hardware access is the inline watchdog kick
column4: so not mc68k_ (commit 16143a5c) (was vp44StatusInitAndWait; PR #53 round 85)

Its only hardware access is the inline watchdog kick
column4: so not mc68k_ (commit 16143a5c) (was vp44_FUN_00027cd0; PR #53 round 85)

column3: The power-down sequence mc68k_applicationMain runs after its background loop ends (ROM 0x289FA; the .cpp shows no caller because Ghidra prunes the main's exit). CM848's cm848_runPowerDownSequence runs the same sequence with the same constants. mc68k_ for its CTM4_BIUTBR reads (was vp44_FUN_00027f9c; PR #53 round 85)

The application main: mc68k_main calls it once (ROM 0x1DCF4) and it never returns. Its start-up clears working RAM (cm550_clearWorkingMemory) after mc68k_loadTpuMicrocode - copies the calibration (cm550_copyCalibrationFromRomToRam) - loads a parameter block - and configures the QSM / SIM / TPU / CTM4 interrupts and channels; then it runs the background loop and mc68k_runPowerDownSequence. 0x28978 inside it is the restart entry cm550_restartOnKeyOnDuringPowerDown jumps to. CM848's cm848_applicationMain has the same skeleton (was vp44_FUN_000284e8; PR #53 round 85)

Initializes the J1939 datalink on the chip select 4 82527: the CAN transmit / receive ring pointers - the transport frame buffers - a 4-entry source address list of 0xFE - 21 transmit buffer initializers - 19 periodic schedule entries - and the remaining set-up / registration calls. Its old shared name came from a pairing CM848 later dropped (was initDiagnosticBufferPointers; PR #53 round 85)

Initializes the J1708 datalink: the secure write scratch pad - the diagnostic buffer pointers (cm550_diagnosticBufferPointerInit) - the J1708 receive state - the multipacket flags - the broadcast enable word (from EEPROM 0x47e) - the InSite parameter schedule (next due ticks from insite_parameter_schedule_table) - then the QSM SCI (QSM_SCCR0 = 0x34 / QSM_SCCR1 = 0x102c). Six startup functions call it (was mc68k_FUN_00029130; PR #53 round 75)

Reprograms the boot block from boot_block_image: when boot_block_version (ROM 0x16) is non-zero and _this_key_must_be_set_to_bad1_before_boot_block_is_programmed_none is 0xbad1 with boot_block_version below boot_block_image_version - or 0x1d1d with a different version - it sets the boot block programming enable flag bit 2 - erases (cm550_flashEraseFromRam(0 / 1)) - and copies 0x291F4 up to this function's address through a 256-byte RAM buffer into flash at address 0 with cm550_flashProgramFromRam (was cm550_FUN_0002ce64; PR #53 round 84)

A PWM output driver read-back fault monitor - nothing in it reads oil pressure or engine speed: for PWM1 / PWM2 / PWM5 with a non-zero period it compares the read-back pin (bit 7 of DASM10SIC / DASM9SIC / DASM4SIC) with the commanded duty - a high pin at 0 % or a low pin at 100 % counts a driver error and the right level heals it. For its first 6 passes it also steps mc68k_waterInFuelDiagnosticHandler (in fact the PWM 3 / 4 start-up check) (was oilPressureRpmFaultMonitor; PR #53 round 85)

Processes a TSC1 (PGN 0) for the engine: the twin of CM848's processEngineTsc1Request (0x22d60). Byte 1 & 3 is the override control mode (SPN 695) and & 0x30 the priority (SPN 897); bytes 2-3 are the requested speed and byte 4 the requested torque. Rejects senders through cm550_diagnosticMessageValidator / cm550_diagnosticSessionValidator (the twins of CM848's ignored request and source configuration lookups) (was torqueControlModeHandler)

Unscrambles the 10-byte security key: each bit goes to the front of the work buffer when its security_key_scramble_mask bit is 0 and to the back otherwise / each work byte is XORed with the work byte its security_key_byte_order entry names / the output is written through security_key_byte_order backwards. The same function and tables as CM848 0x555cc / 0x5839a / 0x583a4 (shared name; was cm550_FUN_0002fbd8; PR #53 round 72).

Checks the 10-byte security key of a secured request: 0 (pass) when calibration_download_security_key_cal is 0xff; 1 once security_key_failure_count reaches 0x11 (a lockout after 17 misses); else unscrambleSecurityKey gives 6 characters (compared with security_master_password_cal) and a 4-byte hour meter stamp ((meter & ~0xff) - (stamp & ~0xff) < 0x1a): a match clears the count and passes / a miss adds one and fails. Called by writeJ1939DiagnosticMemory (types 3 / 5) and mc68k_dispatchJ1708ReceivedMessages (J1708 command 3). The same function as CM848 0x5573c (shared name; was sensorRangeValidation; PR #53 round 72).

The CTM4 MCSM11 interrupt handler of the J1708 driver (no caller - reached through the vector table): clears CTM4_MCSM11SIC's interrupt level and bit 15 and j1708_bus_timer_armed_flag - closes the received message (drops messages of fewer than 3 bytes and checks j1708_message_checksum) - and writes a pending transmit byte to QSM_SCDR. It drives no TPU channel (was mc68k_tpuChannelStateMachine; PR #53 round 77)

Sets up TPU channel 12: clears its priority / interrupt enable / interrupt status - function 0xb (CFSR0 bits 3-0) - parameter 0 = 0x92 - parameters 2-3 = 0xffff - host service request 2 - priority 1. Then it computes _tach_output_minimum_rpm
column4: so the channel may be the tachometer output (not checked). No CAN register is involved (was mc68k_can1ControllerInit; PR #53 round 82)
